<!--
This script runs the actual compiled fusion_update tools and the actual
legacy FUSION v4.40 install side by side on the same real point-cloud files,
timing each run with proc.time() and reporting whatever numbers come out --
favorable or not. It replaces the "Section 5: Speed Benchmarks" table that
previously lived in fusion_evaluation_report.qmd, which was a hand-entered
data.frame of illustrative numbers, not a measurement of anything.

Run this after any update that touches performance-sensitive code (raster
sampling, point-cloud I/O, per-cell metric accumulation, smoothing/filtering
passes) -- not just after a change explicitly described as a speed fix.
Re-running it is the only way to know whether a change actually moved wall-
clock time, in either direction.

Chunk-by-chunk pipeline script per r_coding_standards.md Section 19 -- "#
Step N" headings in execution order, no Data/Methods/Results skeleton. It
still renders to HTML (like its sibling fusion_evaluation_report.qmd in this
same folder) because the point of this particular script is a shareable
benchmark report, not just a diagnostic run.
-->

## Reset working directory to the project root

<!--
This script lives in tests/R/, but Quarto executes chunks with the working
directory set to the .qmd's own folder by default. Project-relative paths
below are written relative to fusion_update/ (two levels up).
-->

```{r}
#| label: root-dir

knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = file.path("..", ".."))
```

## Load libraries and set default options

```{r}
#| label: setup

library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(terra)
library(RForInvt)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
    echo      = TRUE
  , warning   = FALSE
  , message   = FALSE
  )

options(scipen = 10E6)

dir_scratch = file.path("scratch", "benchmark")
dir_out     = file.path("tests", "R", "output")
dir.create(dir_scratch, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(dir_out, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## Define helper functions used throughout this benchmark

```{r}
#| label: helper-functions

# Runs one executable with the given arguments and returns its real
# wall-clock elapsed time (seconds) via proc.time(), along with its exit
# status and captured output. Does not parse or trust any "elapsed time"
# string the tool itself prints -- those differ in rounding/precision
# between the legacy and updated tools and are not what gets reported here.
fn_run_timed = function(exe_path, args, label){
  #1. resolve the executable to an absolute path -- system2() cannot resolve
  #   a relative "../.." executable path reliably on Windows
  exe_path_abs = normalizePath(exe_path, mustWork = TRUE)

  #2. run the command, capturing wall-clock time around it
  time_start = proc.time()
  out = tryCatch(
      system2(exe_path_abs, args = args, stdout = TRUE, stderr = TRUE)
    , error = function(e) paste("ERROR:", conditionMessage(e))
    )
  time_elapsed = (proc.time() - time_start)[["elapsed"]]
  status = attr(out, "status")
  if(is.null(status)) status = 0L

  #3. report failures immediately rather than silently recording a bogus time
  if(status != 0){
    warning(paste0(label, " exited with status ", status, ":\n", paste(tail(out, 10), collapse = "\n")))
    }

  list(elapsed_sec = time_elapsed, status = status, output = out)
  }

# Builds a ground-surface DEM for one input point cloud in both formats
# needed for a fair comparison: a GeoTIFF (fusion_update's /ground: input)
# and a PLANS DTM (legacy FUSION's positional groundfile argument), derived
# from the *same* underlying ground raster so both tools normalize against
# equivalent terrain rather than two independently-filtered surfaces. This
# setup step is not timed -- only the CanopyModel/GridMetrics runs below are.
fn_build_matched_ground = function(las_path, tag, cellsize, dir_scratch, dir_bin_new, dir_legacy){
  #1. run fusion_update's groundfilter to get a GeoTIFF ground DEM
  path_tif = file.path(dir_scratch, paste0("ground_", tag, ".tif"))
  system2(
      normalizePath(file.path(dir_bin_new, "groundfilter.exe"), mustWork = TRUE)
    , args = c(shQuote(las_path), paste0("/output-raster:", path_tif), paste0("/cellsize:", cellsize))
    , stdout = FALSE
    )
  if(!file.exists(path_tif)) stop("fn_build_matched_ground: groundfilter.exe did not produce ", path_tif)

  #2. export that raster as an ESRI ASCII grid (drop the CRS -- legacy
  #   ASCII2DTM takes coordinate system as separate numeric switches, not a
  #   CRS string, and a CRS tag on the ASCII header is not something it reads)
  path_asc = file.path(dir_scratch, paste0("ground_", tag, ".asc"))
  r = terra::rast(path_tif)
  terra::crs(r) = ""
  terra::writeRaster(r, path_asc, filetype = "AAIGrid", overwrite = TRUE)

  #3. convert the ASCII grid into a legacy PLANS DTM -- xyunits/zunits = M
  #   (meters), coordsys/zone/horizdatum/vertdatum = 0 (unknown); none of
  #   these affect the raster values used for height normalization, only
  #   metadata legacy FUSION stores in the DTM header
  path_dtm = file.path(dir_scratch, paste0("ground_", tag, ".dtm"))
  system2(
      normalizePath(file.path(dir_legacy, "ASCII2DTM64.exe"), mustWork = TRUE)
    , args = c(path_dtm, "M", "M", "0", "0", "0", "0", path_asc)
    , stdout = FALSE
    )
  if(!file.exists(path_dtm)) stop("fn_build_matched_ground: ASCII2DTM64.exe did not produce ", path_dtm)

  list(tif = path_tif, dtm = path_dtm)
  }
```

# Benchmark overview

This script times the real, compiled `fusion_update` tools against the real, installed legacy FUSION v4.40 tools (`C:/FUSION`), on two real point-cloud tiles already shipped with this project -- a ~52K-point 200ft clip and a ~6.1M-point full tile. It reports actual `proc.time()` wall-clock seconds, not estimates.

Two comparisons, chosen because both sides expose the same CLI switch with the same meaning, so the two tools are asked to do genuinely comparable work:

1. **CanopyModel smoothing** (Step 4) -- isolates the exact fix in commit `794f79f` (O(W^2) brute-force smoothing replaced by a separable O(W) filter). No ground surface needed; both tools take the same `/smooth:<W>` switch.
2. **GridMetrics, ground-normalized** (Step 5) -- exercises the raster-sampling cache fix from commit `6afb2cc` by supplying both tools a ground surface derived from the same source raster. This comparison is **not** apples-to-apples in scope, and Step 5 says why before showing any numbers.

```{r}
#| label: locate-tools-and-data

#1. legacy FUSION v4.40 install and this repo's freshly-built tools --
#   deliberately the build/ tree, not bin/: bin/ is a periodically-refreshed
#   packaged snapshot (stale by design between packaging runs) and would
#   silently benchmark old code after a same-day fix. build.ps1 now builds
#   outside Box Sync by default (see its -LocalRoot parameter and comment --
#   real timed comparisons showed Box Sync adds erratic multi-second
#   overhead to launching these statically-linked GDAL binaries), so that
#   local location is checked first; the repo-relative build/ directory
#   (what a bare `cmake -B build` still produces) is the fallback for a
#   manual dev build that bypassed build.ps1.
dir_legacy = "C:/FUSION"
dir_bin_new_local = file.path(Sys.getenv("LOCALAPPDATA"), "fusion_update_build", "build")
dir_bin_new = if(file.exists(file.path(dir_bin_new_local, "canopymodel.exe"))) dir_bin_new_local else "build"
if(!dir.exists(dir_legacy)) stop("Legacy FUSION install not found at ", dir_legacy)
if(!file.exists(file.path(dir_bin_new, "canopymodel.exe"))) stop(
  "fusion_update build not found under ", dir_bin_new_local, " or build/ -- build the project first (.\\build.ps1).")
cat("Using fusion_update build at:", dir_bin_new, "\n")

#2. the two real sample point clouds used as the small/large size tiers
path_las_small = file.path("..", "FUSION2-examples", "data", "raw", "lidar",
                            "USGS_LPC_WA_6County_A24_w2049750n409500_clip200ft_las12.las")
path_las_large = file.path("test_output", "USGS_uncompressed.las")
if(!file.exists(path_las_small)) stop("Small sample LAS not found: ", path_las_small)
if(!file.exists(path_las_large)) stop("Large sample LAS not found: ", path_las_large)

dt_datasets = data.table(
    tier     = c("small_52K_pts", "large_6.1M_pts")
  , path_las = c(path_las_small, path_las_large)
  )
print(dt_datasets)
```

# Step 3: Build matched ground surfaces for each dataset tier

Both CanopyModel's `/slope`/`/ground` path and GridMetrics require a ground surface to normalize heights; Step 5 needs one in each tool's native format. Building these is real I/O work but is not part of what's being timed below, so it happens once per tier here, ahead of any timed run.

```{r}
#| label: step-3-build-ground

cellsize_ground = 2.0
list_ground = list()
for(tier_i in dt_datasets$tier){
  las_path_i = dt_datasets[tier == tier_i, path_las]
  list_ground[[tier_i]] = fn_build_matched_ground(
      las_path    = las_path_i
    , tag         = tier_i
    , cellsize    = cellsize_ground
    , dir_scratch = dir_scratch
    , dir_bin_new = dir_bin_new
    , dir_legacy  = dir_legacy
    )
  cat("Built matched ground surfaces for", tier_i, "\n")
  }
```

# Step 4: Time CanopyModel's smoothing filter -- legacy vs. fusion_update

`/smooth:<W>` runs the exact code path rewritten in commit `794f79f`. Window size is swept from 5 to 21 because the separable filter's advantage over the brute-force O(W^2) scan grows with W -- a real speedup should widen, not just appear, as W increases. Repetition count is lower for the large tile purely because each of its runs already takes tens of seconds; the small tile gets more repetitions since each one is cheap.

```{r}
#| label: step-4-canopymodel-benchmark

window_sizes = c(5, 11, 21)
reps_by_tier = c(small_52K_pts = 3L, large_6.1M_pts = 2L)

list_cm_rows = list()
row_i = 0L
for(tier_i in dt_datasets$tier){
  las_path_i = dt_datasets[tier == tier_i, path_las]
  n_reps_i = reps_by_tier[[tier_i]]

  for(window_i in window_sizes){
    for(rep_i in seq_len(n_reps_i)){

      #1. time the legacy CanopyModel run (positional args, disposable .dtm output)
      path_legacy_out = file.path(dir_scratch, paste0("legacy_chm_", tier_i, "_w", window_i, "_r", rep_i, ".dtm"))
      res_legacy = fn_run_timed(
          file.path(dir_legacy, "canopymodel64.exe")
        , args = c(paste0("/smooth:", window_i), path_legacy_out, "1.0", "M", "M", "0", "0", "0", "0", shQuote(las_path_i))
        , label = paste("legacy canopymodel", tier_i, "W =", window_i)
        )

      #2. time the fusion_update CanopyModel run (same window, same input)
      path_new_out = file.path(dir_scratch, paste0("new_chm_", tier_i, "_w", window_i, "_r", rep_i, ".tif"))
      res_new = fn_run_timed(
          file.path(dir_bin_new, "canopymodel.exe")
        , args = c(shQuote(las_path_i), paste0("/smooth:", window_i), "/cellsize:1.0", paste0("/output:", path_new_out))
        , label = paste("fusion_update canopymodel", tier_i, "W =", window_i)
        )

      row_i = row_i + 1L
      list_cm_rows[[row_i]] = data.table(
          benchmark = "canopymodel_smooth", tier = tier_i, window = window_i, rep = rep_i
        , tool = c("legacy", "fusion_update"), elapsed_sec = c(res_legacy$elapsed_sec, res_new$elapsed_sec)
        )
      }
    }
  }
dt_canopymodel_times = rbindlist(list_cm_rows)

#3. verify every timed run produced a finite, positive elapsed time before
#   anything downstream summarizes it
if(any(!is.finite(dt_canopymodel_times$elapsed_sec) | dt_canopymodel_times$elapsed_sec <= 0)){
  stop("step-4: one or more CanopyModel timed runs produced a non-positive or non-finite elapsed time.")
  }
print(dt_canopymodel_times[, .(mean_sec = mean(elapsed_sec)), by = .(tier, window, tool)])
```

# Step 5: Time GridMetrics -- legacy vs. fusion_update, ground-normalized and feature-matched

Both tools are given the same height-strata and intensity-strata thresholds (legacy FUSION's own documented defaults: `/strata:0.15,1.37,5,10,20,30`, `/intstrata:0.25,1.37`), and intensity metrics are turned on for both -- neither side uses `/nointensity`. This closes the metric-bundle gap Step 5 previously flagged. A second, separate gap remains: the two tools default to different *output formats* -- legacy defaults to CSV-only (no raster unless `/raster:` is given); `fusion_update` defaults to writing a multiband GeoTIFF raster alongside its CSV. Rather than force one tool into the other's shape, both output modes are timed explicitly on both tools:

1. **`csv_only`** -- legacy's own CSV-only default vs. `fusion_update` with `/noraster /output-table:<path>.csv` (verified this genuinely suppresses the raster, not just the CLI help text's claim).
2. **`raster_and_csv`** -- legacy with `/raster:<29 matching stat layers>` (its closest equivalent to `fusion_update`'s multiband stat bundle) vs. `fusion_update`'s own raster+CSV default.

Neither arm is a perfect band-for-band match (legacy writes one PLANS DTM file per requested layer; `fusion_update` writes one multiband GeoTIFF plus per-return-type/strata columns a flat layer list doesn't have an equivalent for) -- but both arms now measure real, comparable-scope work on both sides, not one tool's minimal default against the other's maximal one. The large tile's runs take tens of seconds to minutes each, so they get fewer repetitions than the small tile.

```{r}
#| label: step-5-gridmetrics-benchmark

heightbreak = 5.0
cellsize_metrics = 2.0
strata_thresholds = "0.15,1.37,5,10,20,30"       # legacy FUSION's own documented default
intstrata_thresholds = "0.25,1.37"               # legacy FUSION's own documented default
legacy_raster_layers = paste(c(
    "min", "max", "mean", "stddev", "variance", "cv", "mode", "skewness", "kurtosis", "aad"
  , "p01", "p05", "p10", "p20", "p25", "p30", "p40", "p50", "p60", "p70", "p75", "p80", "p90", "p95", "p99"
  , "iq", "cover", "count", "densitytotal"
  ), collapse = ",")
output_modes = c("csv_only", "raster_and_csv")
reps_by_tier_gm = c(small_52K_pts = 3L, large_6.1M_pts = 1L)

list_gm_rows = list()
row_i = 0L
for(tier_i in dt_datasets$tier){
  las_path_i = dt_datasets[tier == tier_i, path_las]
  ground_i = list_ground[[tier_i]]
  n_reps_i = reps_by_tier_gm[[tier_i]]

  for(output_mode_i in output_modes){
    for(rep_i in seq_len(n_reps_i)){

      #1. time the legacy GridMetrics run -- CSV-only is legacy's own default (no
      #   extra switch needed); raster_and_csv adds /raster: on top of that same default
      path_legacy_out = file.path(dir_scratch, paste0("legacy_gm_", tier_i, "_", output_mode_i, "_r", rep_i))
      legacy_args = c(
          paste0("/strata:", strata_thresholds), paste0("/intstrata:", intstrata_thresholds)
        , ground_i$dtm, as.character(heightbreak), as.character(cellsize_metrics)
        , path_legacy_out, shQuote(las_path_i)
        )
      if(output_mode_i == "raster_and_csv"){
        legacy_args = c(paste0("/raster:", legacy_raster_layers), legacy_args)
        }
      res_legacy = fn_run_timed(
          file.path(dir_legacy, "gridmetrics64.exe")
        , args = legacy_args
        , label = paste("legacy gridmetrics", tier_i, output_mode_i)
        )

      #2. time the fusion_update GridMetrics run -- raster_and_csv is fusion_update's
      #   own default (no extra switch needed); csv_only adds /noraster + /output-table
      new_outroot = paste0("new_gm_", tier_i, "_", output_mode_i, "_r", rep_i)
      new_args = c(
          shQuote(las_path_i), paste0("/ground:", ground_i$tif), paste0("/cellsize:", cellsize_metrics)
        , paste0("/minht:", heightbreak), paste0("/strata:", strata_thresholds), paste0("/intstrata:", intstrata_thresholds)
        , paste0("/outdir:", dir_scratch), paste0("/outroot:", new_outroot)
        )
      if(output_mode_i == "csv_only"){
        new_args = c(new_args, "/noraster", paste0("/output-table:", file.path(dir_scratch, paste0(new_outroot, "_table.csv"))))
        }
      res_new = fn_run_timed(
          file.path(dir_bin_new, "gridmetrics.exe")
        , args = new_args
        , label = paste("fusion_update gridmetrics", tier_i, output_mode_i)
        )

      row_i = row_i + 1L
      list_gm_rows[[row_i]] = data.table(
          benchmark = "gridmetrics_ground_normalized", tier = tier_i, window = NA_real_
        , output_mode = output_mode_i, rep = rep_i
        , tool = c("legacy", "fusion_update"), elapsed_sec = c(res_legacy$elapsed_sec, res_new$elapsed_sec)
        )
      }
    }
  }
dt_gridmetrics_times = rbindlist(list_gm_rows)

if(any(!is.finite(dt_gridmetrics_times$elapsed_sec) | dt_gridmetrics_times$elapsed_sec <= 0)){
  stop("step-5: one or more GridMetrics timed runs produced a non-positive or non-finite elapsed time.")
  }
print(dt_gridmetrics_times[, .(mean_sec = mean(elapsed_sec)), by = .(tier, output_mode, tool)])
```

# Step 6: Summarize measured timings and compute speedup factors

Speedup factors below are `legacy mean / fusion_update mean`, computed from the measured means above -- not looked up, not assumed. A factor below 1.0 means `fusion_update` was slower for that configuration, and is reported as such rather than omitted.

```{r}
#| label: step-6-summarize

#1. combine both benchmarks into one long table
dt_all_times = rbind(dt_canopymodel_times, dt_gridmetrics_times, fill = TRUE)

#2. mean/sd/n per benchmark x tier x window x output_mode x tool -- output_mode
#   is NA for the canopymodel rows (that benchmark has no output-format split)
dt_summary_long = dt_all_times[
    , .(mean_sec = mean(elapsed_sec), sd_sec = sd(elapsed_sec), n_reps = .N)
    , by = .(benchmark, tier, window, output_mode, tool)
    ]

#3. reshape legacy vs. fusion_update onto one row per configuration, then
#   compute the real speedup factor from those measured means
dt_summary_wide = dcast(
    dt_summary_long
  , benchmark + tier + window + output_mode ~ tool
  , value.var = c("mean_sec", "sd_sec", "n_reps")
  )
dt_summary_wide[, speedup_factor := round(mean_sec_legacy / mean_sec_fusion_update, 2)]

#4. flag any configuration with only one repetition -- sd_sec is NA there,
#   so a reader isn't misled into thinking that number was more stable than
#   it actually is
dt_summary_wide[n_reps_legacy <= 1 | n_reps_fusion_update <= 1
                , note := "single repetition -- no variability estimate"]

print(dt_summary_wide)
```

# Step 7: Save results and plot measured timings

The full per-run timing table and the summarized speedup table are both saved as versioned CSVs -- the per-run table so a future comparison can pool results across benchmark runs, the summary table as the number a reader actually cites.

```{r}
#| label: step-7-save-and-plot

#1. save the raw per-run timings and the summary table
path_raw = RForInvt::file_version(
    file.path(dir_out, "speed_benchmark_raw_timings.csv")
  , increment = TRUE
  , note = "canopymodel smoothing + gridmetrics ground-normalized runs"
  )
fwrite(dt_all_times, path_raw)

path_summary = RForInvt::file_version(
    file.path(dir_out, "speed_benchmark_summary.csv")
  , increment = TRUE
  , note = "mean/sd elapsed seconds and speedup factor by configuration"
  )
fwrite(dt_summary_wide, path_summary)

#2. mean-elapsed-seconds labels for each box, positioned just above that
#   box's own tallest point -- with as few as 1-3 reps per cell, box height
#   alone is hard to compare across free-scaled facets, so the exact
#   measured mean is printed directly above every box regardless of scale
tool_short_name = c(legacy = "legacy", fusion_update = "update")
dt_cm_labels = dt_canopymodel_times[
    , .(y_label = max(elapsed_sec) * 1.08, label_text = paste0(tool_short_name[tool], "\n", round(mean(elapsed_sec), 1), "s"))
    , by = .(tier, window, tool)
    ]
dt_gm_labels = dt_gridmetrics_times[
    , .(y_label = max(elapsed_sec) * 1.08, label_text = paste0(tool_short_name[tool], "\n", round(mean(elapsed_sec), 1), "s"))
    , by = .(tier, output_mode, tool)
    ]

#3. plot CanopyModel elapsed time by window size and tool, faceted by tier
p_canopymodel = ggplot(dt_canopymodel_times, aes(x = factor(window), y = elapsed_sec, fill = tool)) +
  geom_boxplot(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(
      data = dt_cm_labels
    , aes(x = factor(window), y = y_label, label = label_text, group = tool)
    , position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), size = 3.2, fontface = "bold", show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
  facet_wrap(~tier, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.18))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(legacy = "#94A3B8", fusion_update = "#2563EB")) +
  labs(title = "CanopyModel /smooth: elapsed time", x = "Smoothing window (W)", y = "Elapsed seconds (measured)", fill = "Codebase")

#4. plot GridMetrics elapsed time by tier, output mode, and tool
p_gridmetrics = ggplot(dt_gridmetrics_times, aes(x = tier, y = elapsed_sec, fill = tool)) +
  geom_boxplot(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(
      data = dt_gm_labels
    , aes(x = tier, y = y_label, label = label_text, group = tool)
    , position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), size = 3.2, fontface = "bold", show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
  facet_wrap(~output_mode, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.18))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(legacy = "#94A3B8", fusion_update = "#2563EB")) +
  labs(title = "GridMetrics elapsed time -- height strata + intensity matched on both tools (Step 5)",
       x = "Dataset tier", y = "Elapsed seconds (measured)", fill = "Codebase")

p_combined = p_canopymodel / p_gridmetrics

#4. save the figure, then display it immediately
path_fig = RForInvt::file_version(
    file.path(dir_out, "speed_benchmark.tif")
  , increment = TRUE
  , note = "measured elapsed-time comparison, legacy vs. fusion_update"
  )
ggplot2::ggsave(path_fig, p_combined, device = "tiff", width = 9, height = 9, dpi = 400, compression = "lzw")
shell.exec(normalizePath(path_fig))

p_combined
```
